author: Jon Manley
title: Golf course review: pristine course in Lakewood flying under the radar - NewsBreak
text:
By Jon Manley ,
16 hours ago TNT sports reporter Jon Manley reviews Oakbrook Golf Club in Lakewood, Washington in July 2026.
Jon Manley/Jon Manley / jon.manley@thenewstribune.com
Editor’s note: This review is part of a series, in which TNT sports reporter Jon Manley is playing and reviewing every public golf course in Pierce County. Reviews published so far: Eagle’s Pride (DuPont) | The Classic (Spanaway) | Cedar Irons (Tacoma) | Allenmore (Tacoma)
I’ve played Oakbrook before. I don’t remember it ever being quite this nice.
There were several moments during Friday morning’s round where I just had to stop, look around, and take it all in. The course was in pristine condition, the best I’ve seen. The greens, which are a staple at the Lakewood golf course, were flawless.
The sand traps were pillowy soft (almost too soft, I discovered during a particularly frustrating sequence on hole No. 3). The fairways, rough, tee boxes — everything was immaculate. I’m also a sucker for the oak trees lining the property.
Oakbrook is a semi-private club that offers memberships but is open to the general public. Members receive priority access to tee times to the 6,700-yard course, which presents a legitimate challenge. This isn’t a good-drive-and-short-wedge-in course like some of the shorter local public courses. Pars and birdies are earned here, and you’ll use your entire bag, which I love.
Oakbrook, which opened in 1966, operated as a private club until it was opened to the public in 2012. The course is owned by PGA Tour veteran Ryan Moore and his family. Todd Erwin is the club’s head pro.
Golfing with friends Justin Schauer and Matt Williams, I walked away with a par on the first hole and thought maybe I’d have my way with the course. It quickly humbled me.
Oakbrook forces you to play smart. The course is designed to punish aggressive decisions in certain places. An errant drive can quickly snowball into a triple bogey on several of the holes. It’s a solid challenge and I’m betting most of the members don’t tire of playing the course.
The greens rolled fast and smooth and some of the pin placements on the course created challenging putting scenarios.
I regrouped on the back nine and ended the round with a birdie to shoot an even 90. It wasn’t my finest round of golf, but we had a good time and we all agreed the course was in fantastic shape.
Complaints? The price is a little high (it hovers between $69 and $86 for morning tee times, depending on the day) and the scenery is a little redundant with all the houses lining most of the holes.
Other than that, nothing negative to report. I’d recommend Oakbrook without hesitation in its current form.
THE REVIEW Pros: Pristine from tee to green, the best public course greens in the area, lush fairways, picturesque oak trees, long and challenging, charming post-round patio and restaurant.
Cons: Value could be better, scenery is sometimes redundant winding through residential areas.
MANLEY’S SCORE Quality: 8
Value: 6
Overall: 7
